sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，这是一个我们探讨 20 多岁时重大人生变化和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你在世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能在这里。

sentences.en: You specifically.
sentences.zh: 就是你。

sentences.en: No one else.
sentences.zh: 没有别人。

sentences.en: Back for another episode.
sentences.zh: 又回来收听新的一集了。

sentences.en: Maybe it's your first episode.
sentences.zh: 也许这是你的第一集。

sentences.en: I'm not sure, but welcome.
sentences.zh: 我不确定，但欢迎你。

sentences.en: Welcome as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到我们剖析 20 多岁心理的节目。

sentences.en: I think we all know the feeling of having an amazing conversation with a friend, with someone you've just met, with your partner.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都知道那种感觉，与朋友、刚认识的人或伴侣进行了一次精彩的交谈。

sentences.en: The minutes just float by.
sentences.zh: 时间飞逝。

sentences.en: You feel so aligned and in sync.
sentences.zh: 你感到非常契合和同步。

sentences.en: You're excited.
sentences.zh: 你很兴奋。

sentences.en: You're buzzing with this energy, like someone is kind of like put a mirror in front of us and is reflecting back all of these deep beliefs and funny anecdotes and stories,
sentences.zh: 你沉浸在这种能量中，就像有人在我们面前放了一面镜子，映照出我们所有深层的信念、有趣的轶事和故事，

sentences.en: making us feel seen and heard, but also being like very entertaining, maybe deep.
sentences.zh: 让我们感到被看见、被倾听，同时也觉得非常有趣，甚至深刻。

sentences.en: It is a certain kind of high and one that I want all of us to have more often.
sentences.zh: 这是一种特定的快感，我希望我们所有人都能更频繁地拥有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Conversations really unlock some of the best things about us.
sentences.zh: 对话确实能激发我们身上最美好的一些特质。

sentences.en: Our capacity to share knowledge and to learn, to be vulnerable, to show deep emotion, to connect, to be persuasive or likable.
sentences.zh: 我们分享知识和学习的能力，去脆弱，去展现深层情感，去连接，去变得有说服力或讨人喜欢。

sentences.en: But whilst talking to others may seem like it should just be like one of the easiest things in the world, that is not always the case.
sentences.zh: 但是，虽然与他人交谈看起来应该是世界上最简单的事情之一，但事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Whether you are naturally shy, you're dealing with social anxiety, you've kind of just lost a bit of your spark and simply need a reminder of what connects us to others.
sentences.zh: 无论你是天生害羞，正在应对社交焦虑，还是仅仅失去了一点活力，需要提醒自己是什么将我们与他人联系在一起。

sentences.en: Sometimes we do need to be reminded and have a bit of a refresher on what makes a good conversation.
sentences.zh: 有时我们确实需要被提醒，并温习一下什么才是好的对话。

sentences.en: I also think listening and communicating is something that we can all get better at.
sentences.zh: 我也认为倾听和沟通是我们所有人都可以改进的地方。

sentences.en: It is such a valuable skill to be able to talk to anyone you meet and not just talk but actually connect.
sentences.zh: 能够与你遇到的任何人交谈，而且不仅仅是交谈，而是真正建立联系，这是一项非常有价值的技能。

sentences.en: Especially in our 20s when there are just so many new people to me and to get to know and the connections that we make now really influence and change our entire lives.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在我们 20 多岁的时候，有那么多新朋友需要认识，而我们现在建立的联系确实会影响并改变我们的整个人生。

sentences.en: And this is the skill to have of them all.
sentences.zh: 这是所有技能中最重要的一项。

sentences.en: It's so applicable to every area of your life to be a good conversationalist to your dating life, making friends, job interviews, networking.
sentences.zh: 成为一个好的谈话者适用于你生活的方方面面：约会、结交朋友、求职面试、社交。

sentences.en: So let's talk about it today.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: How can we have better conversations?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能进行更好的对话？

sentences.en: What makes some people so easy to talk to?
sentences.zh: 是什么让有些人那么容易交谈？

sentences.en: Why do we click more with them than others and what are their secrets?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们与他们比与其他人更投缘，他们的秘诀是什么？

sentences.en: How can we learn from them?
sentences.zh: 我们如何向他们学习？

sentences.en: On top of that, what does the psychology and the science really say about good conversations?
sentences.zh: 除此之外，心理学和科学对好的对话到底是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Is the secret listening?
sentences.zh: 秘诀是倾听吗？

sentences.en: Is it body language?
sentences.zh: 是肢体语言吗？

sentences.en: Is it specific questions or pauses?
sentences.zh: 是特定的问题还是停顿？

sentences.en: There are entire careers that have been established on investigating this very question.
sentences.zh: 已经有整个职业是建立在研究这个问题之上的。

sentences.en: So I have five tips for you today to have the best connections and conversations you have ever had, a bit of a formula for when it's tricky and essentially how we can control,
sentences.zh: 所以我今天有五个建议给你，让你拥有有史以来最好的连接和对话，当情况棘手时，这算是一个公式，本质上是我们如何控制，

sentences.en: you know, our interactions and the things that we can control about our interactions and our conversations to make them deep and meaningful and amazing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的互动，以及我们在互动和对话中可以控制的事情，让它们变得深刻、有意义且美妙。

sentences.en: So if you know me, you know I love a big old chat and I am so pumped for this episode and I honestly learned so much that I can apply to my own life.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你了解我，你就知道我喜欢长谈，我对这一集感到非常兴奋，老实说，我学到了很多可以应用到自己生活中的东西。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 所以事不宜迟，让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Good conversations don't always come naturally.
sentences.zh: 好的对话并不总是自然而然发生的。

sentences.en: That is a fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个事实。

sentences.en: It's so interesting because we are never taught how to have good conversations.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我们从未被教导如何进行好的对话。

sentences.en: We are just kind of expected to pick it up along the way and get accustomed to the kind of rules of engagement.
sentences.zh: 我们只是被期望在过程中自然习得，并习惯于某种互动规则。

sentences.en: Make eye contact.
sentences.zh: 进行眼神交流。

sentences.en: Find something we have in common.
sentences.zh: 找到共同点。

sentences.en: Don't stray too far from what's relevant.
sentences.zh: 不要偏离主题太远。

sentences.en: Small talk firSt.
sentences.zh: 先进行寒暄。

sentences.en: Sometimes though, something just doesn't click even when we have done it all right.
sentences.zh: 但有时，即使我们做对了一切，事情就是无法产生共鸣。

sentences.en: I have even found that with some of my closest and longest friends there will just be days where it's like trying to fit a triangle through a circle.
sentences.zh: 我甚至发现，即使是我最亲密、认识最久的朋友，也会有那么几天，感觉就像试图把三角形塞进圆形里一样困难。

sentences.en: That can sometimes cause a spiral.
sentences.zh: 这有时会导致情绪螺旋。

sentences.en: You know, this whole line of questioning around whether we're actually compatible or even that close or even get along.
sentences.zh: 你知道，围绕我们是否真的兼容，甚至是否真的亲密，或者是否合得来的一系列质疑。

sentences.en: Because being able to hold an interesting conversation is such a mark of inherent chemistry between two people.
sentences.zh: 因为能够进行有趣的对话是两个人之间内在化学反应的标志。

sentences.en: What we don't always account for are the mental distractions that we are each facing.
sentences.zh: 我们并不总是考虑到我们每个人所面临的心理干扰。

sentences.en: The to-do lists spiraling off in the back of our minds.
sentences.zh: 脑海中不断盘旋的待办事项清单。

sentences.en: The overstimulation or mental exhaustion that sometimes just makes us poor communicators.
sentences.zh: 有时会让我们成为糟糕沟通者的过度刺激或精神疲惫。

sentences.en: So for our first tip, I wanted one that it doesn't really matter what you have going on in the mental background.
sentences.zh: 所以对于第一个建议，我想要一个无论你脑子里在想什么都不太重要的建议。

sentences.en: You can still apply it.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以应用它。

sentences.en: Because conversation isn't just about you, it's about the other person.
sentences.zh: 因为对话不仅仅是关于你，而是关于对方。

sentences.en: Instead of trying so hard to keep the spark alive by just feeling the silences and just saying more, tip number one, ask more questions than you answer.
sentences.zh: 与其通过填补沉默和说更多的话来努力维持火花，建议一：多问问题，少回答问题。

sentences.en: People love talking about themselves, but they love talking about themselves even more when they have something to talk about, when they feel inspired, and when they feel
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢谈论自己，但当他们有话可说、感到受启发、以及感到

sentences.en: listened to.
sentences.zh: 被倾听时，他们更喜欢谈论自己。

sentences.en: The easiest way to trigger all three of these things is to simply ask them a really good question.
sentences.zh: 触发这三件事最简单的方法就是简单地问他们一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: The best communicators and conversationalists are people who understand the two-to-one ratio.
sentences.zh: 最好的沟通者和谈话者是那些理解二比一比例的人。

sentences.en: For every question that they ask you, ask two of your own, whether that's a follow-up question to a previous thing they've said, or to kind of introduce a brand new topic.
sentences.zh: 每当他们问你一个问题时，你就问两个自己的问题，无论是对他们之前所说内容的后续追问，还是引入一个全新的话题。

sentences.en: I know that sounds quite mathematical and very clinical, but a conversation is very much like a scenic walk, or like a very long drive.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来很数学化，也很生硬，但对话非常像一次风景优美的散步，或者一次很长的驾驶。

sentences.en: The best kinds are the ones with twists and turns, with new scenery, with little stops along the way, with new environments, and they're also the best when somebody is driving,
sentences.zh: 最好的对话是那些有曲折、有新风景、沿途有小停靠站、有新环境的对话，而且当有人在驾驶时，它们也是最好的，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: When somebody is guiding you through a conversation, through a new situation, questions are a way to do that.
sentences.zh: 当有人引导你进行对话、经历新情况时，问题就是做到这一点的方法。

sentences.en: And being intentional and deliberate about how much you are talking versus listening, that is really, really valuable.
sentences.zh: 而且在说话和倾听的比例上保持刻意和深思熟虑，这是非常有价值的。

sentences.en: This is actually called a doorknob for psychologists researching conversations.
sentences.zh: 对于研究对话的心理学家来说，这实际上被称为“门把手”。

sentences.en: basically, you know, a very important part of a conversation is providing somebody with, you know, something that they can grab onto that opens up a new space.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你知道，对话中一个非常重要的部分是为某人提供，你知道，他们可以抓住的东西，从而打开一个新的空间。

sentences.en: So a good question is the doorknob.
sentences.zh: 所以一个好的问题就是门把手。

sentences.en: And it is essentially, you've planted it there, but it's a way for somebody else to feel like they are really, you know, accepted and guiding this conversation and that it's taking
sentences.zh: 它本质上是你把它放在那里，但这是让对方觉得他们真的，你知道，被接受并引导着这场对话，并且它正在将

sentences.en: them to a new level.
sentences.zh: 他们带到一个新的水平。

sentences.en: The power of questions might seem quite simple, but at its core, the reason this is so effective comes down to attention.
sentences.zh: 问题的力量看起来很简单，但其核心在于，这种方法之所以如此有效，归根结底是因为关注。

sentences.en: A really great article published by
sentences.zh: 《今日心理学》发表的一篇非常棒的文章

sentences.en: Psychology Today put it really well.
sentences.zh: 很好地阐述了这一点。

sentences.en: Attention has its own magic.
sentences.zh: 关注本身就有魔力。

sentences.en: We as humans crave recognition from others.
sentences.zh: 我们作为人类，渴望得到他人的认可。

sentences.en: And there is a lot of experimental evidence that says being ostracized or ignored by others creates a pain that is every bit as real and intense as physical injury.
sentences.zh: 有大量的实验证据表明，被他人排斥或忽视会产生一种与身体伤害一样真实且强烈的痛苦。

sentences.en: So to counteract that, we should show people that we want to be interested in us and who we are interested in, that we are paying attention to them.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了抵消这一点，我们应该向人们展示我们想要对我们自己以及我们感兴趣的人表现出兴趣，我们正在关注他们。

sentences.en: According to
sentences.zh: 根据

sentences.en: Social Attention
sentences.zh: 社会关注

sentences.en: Holding Potential Theory, which you should really Google, it's very interesting, this is a theory developed by the
sentences.zh: 持有潜力理论（你应该去谷歌搜索一下，非常有趣），这是由英国心理学家

sentences.en: British psychologist
sentences.zh: Paul Gilbert 开发的理论，我们经常倾向于互相竞争以获得他人的关注。

sentences.en: Paul Gilbert, we often tend to compete with each other to have people pay attention to us.
sentences.zh: 当其他人注意到我们时，我们会感觉良好，享受各种积极的情绪：自信、归属感、接纳。

sentences.en: When other people take notice, we feel good, we enjoy all kinds of positive feelings, confidence, belonging, acceptance.
